Gommaṭasāra
Jain. Dig. Pkt. in two sections Jīvakāṇḍa an. Karmakāṇḍa containing 733 an. 972 gāthās respectively; also called Pañcasaṅgraha a. it contains five topics: Bandha, Badhyamāna, Bandhasvāmin, Bandhahetu an. Bandhabheda; the essence of Jaina doctrine explained to Cāmuṇḍarāya, Minister an. general of the Gaṅga princes Mārasim3ha (died 974 A. D.) an. Rācamalla II (974-84 A. D.), an. also called Gommaṭarāya since he erected the colossal statue of Gommaṭa in Śravaṇabelgola, Mysore in about 980 A. D.; by Saiddhāntika Nemicandra, with the help of Kanakanandin; Labdhisāra an. Kṣapaṇāsāra are supplements appended to it.
See Wint. HIL. II. p.. 585-86; A. N. Upadhye, Bhāratīya Vidyā, II. [Page174-a. p.. 48 ff. For the lacunae in Karmakāṇḍa an. its connection with the Karmaprakṛti of Nemicandra, see Anekānt III. p.. 537. 635. 757. 762-3. For G. a. a saṅgrahagrantha see Anekānt III. iv. 298.
